java_locations: PlantUML FileFormat.getJavaDimension (220-238): FontMetrics.getStringBounds(text, gg) on UFontImpl.getUnderlayingFont -> FontStack.getFont (109-122), the first (here the only) family of the stack, derived for the face.

JDK java/awt/Font.getStringBounds(char[], ...) (2614-2650): text is 'simple' unless FontUtilities.isComplexText(chars) (190-201): any UTF-16 surrogate unit (isNonSimpleChar 214-218) or a char with isComplexCharCode (239-311: 0300-036F, 0590-06FF, 0900-0E7F, 0F00-109F, 1100-11FE, 1780-17FF, 200C-200D, 202A-202E, 206A-206F). Simple text is measured by FontDesignMetrics.getSimpleBounds on the Font2D's own mapper; complex text by new TextLayout(str, font, frc).

Simple path, JDK sun/font/CCharToGlyphMapper (macOS): the CFont's glyph, or for a character the font lacks, nativeCharsToGlyphs (98, 134) returns the glyph CoreText substitutes (negative code, 'measures exactly as a real glyph'); 'missing characters for any font on the system will be returned as 0' (missingGlyph = 0, line 39): the primary font's .notdef.

Complex path, JDK sun/font/CFont.createCompositeFont (203-240): slots = the CFont + getCascadeList (CTFontCopyDefaultCascadeListForLanguages) names + 'GeezaPro', each by CFontManager.getOrCreateFallbackFont (328-338: names starting with '.' are dropped; '.AppleSymbolsFB' is renamed AppleSymbols); CCompositeGlyphMapper.convertToGlyph (54-68) takes the first slot whose code is > 0, else missingGlyph (slot 0's .notdef). TextLayout shapes with HarfBuzz, which hides default-ignorable code points (hb _hb_unicode_is_default_ignorable: in planes 1-16 only U+1D173..U+1D17A and U+E0000..U+E0FFF) with zero advance.

Font metric source (environment, read from the font files on the origin Mac through CoreText CTFontGetAdvancesForGlyphs on glyph 0 at 2048 units/em): .notdef advance Lucida Grande 1536 (regular and bold), Arial 1536, Helvetica 1298 / Helvetica Bold 1479, Verdana 2048, Menlo 1233 (= the Monospaced cell, MONO_WIDTH_PER_SIZE), Courier New 1229 (= COURIER_NEW_WIDTH_PER_SIZE); Times New Roman 1593 is already the Java-extracted MISSING_FIXED_UNITS of times_new_roman_unicode.rs.

validation_of_the_chain_model.oracle: times_new_roman_unicode.rs is a Java AWT extraction (tools/PhysicalFontMetricsExtract.java --rust-unicode-ranges): Font.getStringBounds of every scalar Java defines, alone, for Times New Roman. Its MISSING_FIXED_UNITS (1593) marks scalars Java measured with the missing glyph.
validation_of_the_chain_model.method: The extraction tool below applied to Times New Roman predicts, per scalar measured alone: supplementary or isComplexCharCode -> complex path (composite cmap coverage; HarfBuzz default-ignorable -> zero); else simple path (own glyph or CoreText substitution, LastResort/no glyph/user font -> missing).
validation_of_the_chain_model.result: 286,520 of 286,591 Java-defined scalars agree (99.975%). Disagreements: 52 with a Java advance the model calls missing (U+0528..U+052D and similar, fonts changed by later OS updates), 17 Java-missing the model maps (e.g. U+01CC, a glyph whose advance happens to equal 1593 units, or later font additions), U+A69E (Java zero) and U+11FD2. Recorded in maker-round5-claude/measurements/font-chain-validation.json.
validation_of_the_chain_model.consistency_with_sans_table: NON_ASCII_WIDTHS (Java SansSerif advances of 409 corpus scalars): 408 agree with the Lucida Grande chain (mapped, or 0.75 em when missing); U+FE0F is 0.75 em in Java but CoreText substitutes Apple Color Emoji. literal_char_width already gives U+FE0F zero before the table (unchanged).

planned_change: tools/FontChainExtract.swift (environment extraction, not Java): emits per face the BMP runs the simple path cannot map and the runs the complex path maps (complex-BMP ranges and planes 1-16), with each face's .notdef advance in font units. tools/font_chain_coverage.py turns that output into crates/rustuml-render/src/font_chain_coverage.rs (identical run tables shared between faces).
font_chain_coverage::resolve(face, ch, complex_text) -> Mapped | Missing | Hidden, with complex_text = FontUtilities.isComplexText over the measured string's Java units, and notdef_per_em(face).

plantuml_metrics::literal_char_width: after the ASCII table, zero-width joiners, colour emoji and NON_ASCII_WIDTHS (Java-measured), Missing -> Lucida Grande (Bold) .notdef 1536/2048 per size and Hidden -> 0, before the remaining approximations. is_supplementary_private_use and its 0.75 constant are removed (subsumed).

family_table_text_width (Arial, Verdana) and helvetica_text_width: Missing -> that face's .notdef, Hidden -> 0, otherwise unchanged. mono_text_width and courier_new_text_width: Hidden -> 0 (Missing is one cell already, .notdef = cell). Times New Roman keeps its Java table.
unchanged: An unpaired unit keeps one em (AW surrogate_high_class) in the SansSerif paths, one cell in Monospaced/Courier New, and its former table lookup in Times New Roman.
Every Java-measured table (CHAR_WIDTHS_*, NON_ASCII_WIDTHS, Arabic/cluster tables, Times New Roman) takes precedence; mapped scalars outside them keep their approximations.
declared_residue: The coverage is the origin Mac's system fonts (macOS 27.2 here; user fonts in ~/Library/Fonts excluded). The reference runs on Monkey Man (different macOS and JDK 21.0.5); font coverage can differ there. Probes in relay batch m5a measure it.

Serif (Gantt only, 'Times' face) has no chain table; it keeps its approximations.
